title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ཞེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 190)
shelf_note: A Derge woodblock folio (margin volume letter ཞེ) of a Pramāṇa commentary refuting Sāṃkhya (vyakta/prakṛti/vikāra, asiddha and anaikāntika reasons). It belongs in the Tshad ma section of the Tengyur.

tr_errors_A.english: without pointing out or explaining the fault in the proof established by the Sāṃkhya
tr_errors_A.problem: The source names the fault of proving what is already proven (siddhasādhana). A turns it into 'the proof established by the Sāṃkhya', which loses the technical fault the Naiyāyika is blamed for not raising.

tr_errors_A.english: We spoke to the Sāṃkhya precisely through defining this nature of the fault of being unestablished and the characteristics of transformation
tr_errors_A.problem: Misparsed: the source says the opponent stated this very form of the asiddha fault by setting out the definitions of prakṛti and vikāra. A attaches 'nature' to the fault rather than to prakṛti.

tr_errors_A.english: asking: "Now, where are its ears, its feet, and its eyes?"
tr_errors_A.problem: The page breaks off mid-sentence, but A finishes it with an invented 'where are' and a closed question.
ངོ་མཚར་བྱེད means 'performs a marvel/show', not 'creates an illusion'. A gives the reading in advance.
A drops the 'its/that' (the property is contrary to manifestness), which leaves the reason vague.

tr_errors_B.problem: Here གསལ་བ is the Sāṃkhya vyakta, 'the manifest' (as against prakṛti). B renders it 'clarity' throughout, so the argument about the manifest world sharing a nature with pleasure and prakṛti is hard to recognise.

tr_errors_B.english: the claim that clarity and this nature are one and the same
tr_errors_B.problem: Here རང་བཞིན is prakṛti (primordial nature), and 'this' belongs to the manifest. B blurs the thesis being refuted.

tr_errors_B.english: using logical arguments from the Nyaya perspective
tr_errors_B.problem: The page also faults the Naiyāyika. It is not argued from the Nyāya side, so the summary misstates the stance.

tr_errors_B.english: Pleasure and clarity are not of the same nature
tr_errors_B.problem: The alternative 'or' (འམ) that introduces the second argument is dropped.

pages.prefer_reason: A has the right Sāṃkhya terms (manifest, primordial matter) but misreads the siddhasādhana fault and the opponent's statement, and invents the end of the broken sentence. B gets the structure of the debate right but mistranslates vyakta as 'clarity' throughout. Neither has a serious error, and their moderate errors roughly balance.

book_verdict: A clean Derge folio. The OCR follows the print closely as far as I can read it at this resolution. Both English versions are usable, with only moderate terminology or parsing slips and nothing a reader would be misled by on sight.
